messages.subject: scale_x_date empties graph
parts:
Hi,

I have a dataframe with time (POSIXct) and numeric values (double). It
graphs great with:

qplot(time, value, data = df, geom = "step")

However if I add:

+ scale_x_date(c(as.Date("2011-06-01"), as.Date("2011-06-07")))

A plot gets drawn with the right timeframe, but all the data
disappears and I just have an empty graph. (I double checked with the
original graph; there should be something there...)

Why is this?

Thanks in advance!

-Derrick

messages.author: cbda1d998a4e9f7c
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_date empties graph
parts:
Hello Derrick,

It's a seconds vs. days issue I bet.  

My understanding is that as.Date will make it in days from 1/1/1970 and POSIXct will be in seconds.  This will make is so your scales won't match.  Scale your values with 86400 and it might work.

To explore this you can type in as.numeric(as.Date("2011-06-01"))
To explore this you can type in as.numeric(as.POSIXct("2011-06-01"r))

Cheers,
Jonathan

entered:

scale_x_datetime(c(as.POSIXct("2011-06-01"),as.POSIXct("2011-06-07")))

and got a nice graph, but scaled from about May 30 to July 17. This
baffles me greatly, as the args are of course passed in seconds now.
Adding 'origin = "1970-01-01"' does not help either. I will forward a
sample dataframe if requested...

messages.subject: Re: scale_x_date empties graph
parts:
Solved! I forgot to add "limits ="; successful command as follows:

qplot(times, occupancy, data = phase1a, geom = "step") +
scale_x_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("2011-06-01"),
as.POSIXct("2011-06-07")))
